result.verdict: Not ready for build: the Home glance and creation-sheet patterns are promising, but core approval, space-switching, and first-run flows are incomplete or contradictory, Home does not fit one screen, and several states give a first-time founder no recoverable next step.

findings.element: Left rail: black pill, '9:41', 'AB', bell/search pill, '+ New'
findings.problem: The entire global navigation is compressed into an extremely narrow strip. Avatar, bell, and search controls appear well below the 44pt iOS minimum, are icon/initial-only, and the bell's tiny dot does not explain unread count or destination.
findings.norm: iOS HIG: at least 44x44pt targets, recognizable controls, and visible navigation affordances for first-time users.
findings.fix: Widen the rail or move search/profile into the content header; make each control a 44pt labeled target and show an Activity count such as '2 need you'.

findings.element: 'PAGES' list ending in partially visible 'Legal / 2 deadlines'
findings.problem: Home does not fit the 466x678 view. The bottom row is clipped with no scroll indicator, fade, or peek of Cap table/Data room/Team computer, so a founder cannot see all destinations in one glance and may not know scrolling exists.
findings.norm: Persona requirement and mobile convention: primary navigation must either fit one screen or provide an unmistakable scroll cue.
findings.fix: Reduce Activity/Personnel density, collapse Pages to a compact grid, or end the viewport with a deliberate half-row plus fade; test the complete Home hierarchy at 466x678 without ambiguous clipping.

findings.element: 'ACTIVITY' card: 'Finance agent / Approve $1,200 payment / Needs you'
findings.problem: The most urgent item is visually just another status row. It has a chevron but no amount-level action or preview of Approve/Decline, so 'what needs me' does not become a one-tap decision.
findings.norm: Approval UX convention: the blocking item should expose its consequence and primary decision path immediately, especially for payments.
findings.fix: Make Needs you rows visually dominant and open a dedicated approval detail with payee, amount, source, Approve and Decline; do not rely on an unexplained chevron.

findings.element: 'Activity (bell or See all)' board: only populated and 'Empty' states
findings.problem: The board required to open an approval contains no approval detail, loading, error, offline, or completed-approval state. Tapping Finance agent is implied but the actual payment decision is never designed.
findings.norm: State completeness and task closure: every critical entry point needs loading, error, detail, confirmation, and success states.
findings.fix: Add Finance approval detail, approve/decline confirmation, processing, success, failure/retry, loading, and offline states before build.

findings.element: Activity rows 'Legal agent / Working', 'Weekly runway / Done', 'Inbox agent / Done', 'Brex agent / Done'
findings.problem: Only the Needs you row has a chevron; the other rows have no consistent tappability cue and almost no timestamps. Users cannot tell whether Working/Done items open detail or when Earlier items happened.
findings.norm: List convention: identical row types need identical affordances and enough time context to scan history.
findings.fix: Give all navigable rows the same chevron/press state and add time or date to every row; remove chevrons from non-navigable rows.

findings.element: 'Loading' state: skeleton ACTIVITY/PERSONNEL above fully rendered 'PAGES'
findings.problem: Pages look live and tappable while the rest of Home is loading, with no indication whether Inbox '3 need reply' belongs to the current space or stale cache. 'See all' also disappears only from ACTIVITY.
findings.norm: Loading convention: do not present potentially stale navigation data as current; keep section chrome stable during skeleton loading.
findings.fix: Skeleton or clearly badge all stale sections, disable Pages until the space payload resolves, and retain stable section headers.

findings.element: 'Could not load agents': missing ACTIVITY section, 'Could not load agents / Try again' under PERSONNEL
findings.problem: Activity silently vanishes rather than showing its own error, while Pages and Artifacts load normally. The user cannot tell if approvals are unavailable or simply absent—dangerous when a payment may be waiting.
findings.norm: Error design: each failed data domain needs a visible, scoped failure state; absence must never masquerade as 'nothing needs you'.
findings.fix: Show separate Activity and Personnel error rows with retry, preserve a warning that needs-you status is unavailable, and never collapse a failed Activity section.

findings.element: 'Offline, saved data': 'Updated 5 min ago' with active 'Needs you' Finance row
findings.problem: Offline status is only small metadata under Personal. The payment row still looks fully actionable, with no warning that approval cannot sync or may be stale.
findings.norm: Offline convention: cached data and blocked mutations must be explicitly labeled before the user attempts a consequential action.
findings.fix: Add a persistent offline banner, timestamp the Activity data itself, and intercept approval with 'You're offline—this will not send yet' or disable it.

findings.element: 'Empty space': 'No agents yet / New agent' above PAGES with 'Inbox / 3 need reply' and 'Finance / 6 mo runway'
findings.problem: A supposedly empty space still has populated work pages and deadlines, contradicting the empty state and leaving unclear whether the next step is New agent or opening existing Pages.
findings.norm: Empty-state logic: content, counts, and the single next action must agree about whether the workspace has data.
findings.fix: If the space is truly new, empty or hide page counts and keep New agent as the only prominent action; if pages are seeded, rename the state and explain the seeded content.

findings.element: 'New menu': 'New agent', 'New group', 'New space'
findings.problem: 'New space' duplicates the same action in the Personal space switcher, while the menu appears without a scrim or clear anchoring and obscures PAGES. First-time users now have two mental models for creating a space.
findings.norm: Navigation convention: one concept should have one primary creation path; popovers need clear source anchoring and dismissal.
findings.fix: Keep New space only in the space switcher or only in New, add a dim/scrim and menu anchor, and distinguish 'add to this space' from 'create another space'.

findings.element: 'New account, no model': 'Connect a model to start chatting.' above PAGES showing '3 need reply', '6 mo runway', '2 deadlines'
findings.problem: A brand-new account with no model already appears to have email, runway, and legal work. This undermines trust and contradicts the brief's first-run sequence of connect a model, then message Chief.
findings.norm: First-run design: no fabricated operational data before setup; the setup blocker should own the page.
findings.fix: Show empty/locked Pages or remove their counts until connection, keep Chief as the post-connect destination, and leave Connect a model as the sole prominent action.

findings.element: 'Connect a model' sheet: 'API key / Recommended', 'Local server', 'Subscription', privacy text naming 'Model A'
findings.problem: Non-technical founders are asked to understand API keys and local servers with no provider, cost, capability, or Model A definition. 'Model A' appears first in the privacy sentence, after the user must choose.
findings.norm: Consumer onboarding convention: explain the recommended path in plain language before requesting credentials; name the actual service receiving data.
findings.fix: Default to a named guided option such as 'Connect [provider]', explain what an API key is and where to get it, and move Local server under Advanced.

findings.element: 'Connect a model' and 'Key not accepted' states
findings.problem: There is no connecting/validating state, no empty-key disabled state, no paste/show-key affordance, and the error is only 'Key not accepted.' with no cause or recovery step. Connect remains bright white even when retrying the same invalid key is futile.
findings.norm: Form-error convention: validate in context, preserve input, explain likely causes, and provide a specific recovery action.
findings.fix: Add empty, pasting, validating, success, invalid-format, rejected-key, and offline states; include Show/Paste, 'Check for spaces or use a new key', and a help link.

findings.element: 'Switching to Northwind': skeleton ACTIVITY/PERSONNEL but live PAGES 'Inbox / 3 need reply', 'Finance / 6 mo runway'
findings.problem: During a space switch, the previous space's Pages remain presented as Northwind content. A founder could open the wrong company's inbox or finance data.
findings.norm: Multi-workspace safety: tenant context must switch atomically or stale content must be visibly labeled and disabled.
findings.fix: Skeleton/disable the entire content region until Northwind loads; if cache is shown, label it 'Personal—switching…' and block taps.

findings.element: 'Space settings, Personal' bottom-left white check button
findings.problem: Save is an unlabeled check floating in the narrow rail, far from the Name field at the top, and appears enabled even when nothing changed. Its purpose, saved feedback, and keyboard behavior are undiscoverable.
findings.norm: iOS form convention: place a labeled Done/Save action near the form or navigation bar, enable it only when dirty, and confirm saving.
findings.fix: Use 'Save' in the sheet/header near Name, disable it until edited, show keyboard-safe placement, and provide saved confirmation or automatic-save status.

findings.element: 'Space settings, Personal' versus 'Space settings, Northwind': Delete space only on Northwind
findings.problem: Personal has no Delete space and no explanation, while Northwind does. Users cannot tell whether Personal is protected, deletion moved, or the feature is missing.
findings.norm: Settings consistency: conditional destructive actions need an explicit reason when unavailable.
findings.fix: Show 'Delete space' disabled with 'Your default space can't be deleted' on Personal, or state the rule in Space settings.

findings.element: Rail navigation morphing: 'AB' replaced by '<' in Space settings/Activity and by 'X' in Connect a model
findings.problem: Profile identity disappears and back/close controls occupy the avatar's rail position. Back and close also sit at inconsistent vertical positions, weakening spatial memory and making it unclear whether tapping exits, cancels, or opens profile.
findings.norm: Navigation convention: keep global identity/controls stable; reserve consistent locations and symbols for Back versus Close.
findings.fix: Keep the rail constant and place Back/Close in the content header; never reuse the avatar slot for navigation.

findings.element: 'New bot' fields 'Name this bot' and 'What this bot does'; seven-color 'Color' row
findings.problem: A non-technical founder gets no examples, scope, permissions, model choice, or preview of the resulting bot. Color selection is unlabeled beyond hue and the selected teal ring is the only meaning, so users cannot predict how color identifies the bot.
findings.norm: Creation-form convention: provide examples, consequences, and a live preview for identity-defining fields; do not rely on color alone.
findings.fix: Add example role chips/helper text, a live avatar/name preview, color names for accessibility, and state which space and model the bot will use.

findings.element: 'New bot / Creating' and 'Error': active X, spinner replacing 'Create', red text 'Check your connection and retry'
findings.problem: During creation the close X still looks tappable with no cancel consequence, the spinner has no accessible 'Creating…' label, and the error offers no Retry button—the user must infer that Create itself is retry.
findings.norm: Async form convention: label progress, define cancel behavior, preserve data, and provide an explicit retry action at the error.
findings.fix: Disable or confirm X during submission, use spinner plus 'Creating…', and change the error action to a visible 'Try again' while keeping Create's state unambiguous; apply the same fix to New group and New space.

findings.element: 'New group' footer 'Choose 2 to 6 members.' and states '0 selected' / '1 selected' / '2 selected'
findings.problem: The minimum is only discoverable after opening the sheet and Create stays dimmed without saying what remains missing. Only four members are shown, so the 6-member maximum, search, scrolling, and what happens at the limit are never demonstrated.
findings.norm: Constraint design: state required count before selection, update remaining requirement dynamically, and design minimum and maximum boundary states.
findings.fix: Change the helper to live copy such as 'Choose 1 more member', show '2 of 2–6 selected', add search/scroll cues for long lists, and design the 6-selected limit state.

findings.element: 'New space / Empty: Create dimmed' Name field displaying 'Customer support'
findings.problem: The board labeled Empty already contains the same words as the Filled state; only gray versus white text and Create brightness distinguish placeholder from value. At a glance the supposedly empty form looks completed.
findings.norm: Form-state clarity: placeholders must be unmistakably different from entered values and validation must not depend on subtle luminance alone.
findings.fix: Show a truly blank field with placeholder 'e.g. Customer support' in italic/lower-emphasis styling, and verify empty, focused, filled, and error states are distinguishable in grayscale.

findings.element: Creation sheets 'New bot', 'New group', 'New space' over dimmed skeleton background
findings.problem: No keyboard is shown in any state, the destination space is unnamed, and the bottom-half sheet leaves a large dead area in New space. On a real iPhone the keyboard will cover the sheet/error or force a resize that these boards do not specify.
findings.norm: iOS sheet design: specify keyboard avoidance, focus order, scroll behavior, context, and where the primary action remains visible.
findings.fix: Add keyboard-open states for all three siblings, keep Create and field errors above the keyboard, label 'Creating in Personal', and size the New space sheet to its content.

findings.element: Floating elements across Home: bell/search glass pill, '+ New', 'New menu' card, avatar/check/back circular controls
findings.problem: The design rule allows glass only on floating nav/controls and at most three glass groups, but menu-open and settings states accumulate the rail pill, popover card, circular rail controls, and sheet X/Create controls without a clear glass budget. Visual treatments also mix glass, solid dark cards, and bright white pills at similar elevations.
findings.norm: Brief design rule: at most three glass groups per view, glass reserved for floating navigation/controls, solid content surfaces.
findings.fix: Audit each state and annotate the maximum three glass groups; make menus/sheets solid, keep only the rail and its immediate popover floating, and establish one elevation rule.

excellent: PG-A-Home.png — 'Finance agent / Needs you' amber pill is instantly distinguishable from blue 'Working' and green 'Done', giving the correct first-glance priority.
PG-A-Activity.png — 'TODAY' and 'EARLIER' grouping with concise agent outcome lines is clean, scannable, and appropriate between meetings.

PG-B-NewBot.png, PG-B-NewGroup.png, PG-B-NewSpace.png — sibling sheets consistently use X, centered title, top-right Create, dimmed-to-ready Create, spinner, preserved input, and inline error patterns.
PG-B-Spaces.png — 'Delete Northwind?' states 'This removes its agents, chats and files. This cannot be undone.' before the red Delete action; the consequence copy is exemplary.
PG-B-NewSpace.png — 'Name already used' is correctly attached to the Name field with a red field border instead of relying only on a generic banner.
PG-A-HomeNoModel.png — 'After connecting' resolves to exactly one prominent action, 'Message Chief', which matches the intended first-run next step.
PG-B-NewGroup.png — live '0 selected', '1 selected', and '2 selected' counts provide clear progress toward eligibility once the user is inside the form.

result.verdict: Praci’s dark-mode visual language is clean, atmospheric, and disciplined in its typography, but the system suffers from critical cross-board inconsistencies in modal architecture, terminology ('agent' vs. 'bot' vs. 'personnel'), navigation rail persistence, and first-run onboarding logic for a non-technical founder.

findings.element: Modal sheet header and left navigation strip in 'Connect a model' vs. creation sheets
findings.problem: Sheet architecture is contradictory across boards. In PG-A-HomeNoModel.png ('Connect a model' and 'Key not accepted'), the modal sheet has a large left-aligned title, a full-width bottom 'Connect' CTA, and places the close 'X' button outside the sheet in the left hardware strip. In PG-B-NewBot.png, PG-B-NewGroup.png, and PG-B-NewSpace.png, the left strip is emptied and the 'X' close button and 'Create' CTA live inside the sheet's top navigation bar.
findings.norm: All bottom sheets in an iOS app must share a single, predictable header, dismissal, and primary action placement pattern.
findings.fix: Standardize all modal sheets on the in-sheet header pattern (top-left 'X', centered title, or bottom primary button) and remove the orphaned 'X' button from the outer left navigation rail in PG-A-HomeNoModel.png.

findings.element: 'New agent' menu item / button vs. 'New bot' sheet title vs. 'PERSONNEL' section header
findings.problem: The app uses three different nouns for the exact same entity across sibling screens: the section header is 'PERSONNEL', the '+ New' menu item and empty-state button in PG-A-Home.png say 'New agent' ('No agents yet'), and the sheet that opens in PG-B-NewBot.png is titled 'New bot' with placeholders 'Name this bot' and 'What this bot does'.
findings.norm: Core domain objects must use a single canonical term across all labels, menus, empty states, and creation flows.
findings.fix: Pick one term ('Agent' or 'Bot') and use it everywhere—align the section header, the '+ New' menu item, empty/error states, and the creation sheet title and placeholders.

findings.element: 'Connect a model' options list ('API key Recommended', 'Local server', 'Subscription')
findings.problem: The persona is a non-technical first-time founder on a phone between meetings, yet 'API key' is marked 'Recommended' and requires pasting a raw developer key without even specifying which AI provider the key belongs to (later referring to a generic placeholder 'Model A' in the disclaimer and 'Model A connected.' banner).
findings.norm: Onboarding for non-technical mobile users should default to one-tap OAuth/Subscription sign-in and explicitly name the model provider.
findings.fix: Make 'Subscription' (or a named provider sign-in like Claude/OpenAI) the recommended default, provide a clear provider selector when 'API key' is chosen, and replace the placeholder 'Model A' with the actual selected model name.

findings.element: 'PAGES' section in 'New account, no model' (PG-A-HomeNoModel.png), 'Empty space' (PG-A-Home.png), and 'Switching to Northwind' (PG-B-Spaces.png)
findings.problem: Every space and account state displays the exact same hardcoded live metrics in PAGES ('Inbox: 3 need reply', 'Finance: 6 mo runway', 'Legal: 2 deadlines', 'Team computer: Online'), even in 'New account, no model' before any model or data source is connected and in 'Empty space' ('Side project') where 'No agents yet' is shown.
findings.norm: Zero-data and unconfigured states must reflect realistic empty/unconnected states rather than contradicting the top-of-screen state with populated metrics.
findings.fix: Show neutral/empty subtitles in PAGES for 'New account, no model' and 'Empty space' until a model and data sources are connected for that specific space.

findings.element: 'Message Chief' CTA and '+ New' FAB in 'After connecting' state
findings.problem: The 'After connecting' view displays two high-contrast solid white primary buttons simultaneously ('Message Chief' in the top banner card and '+ New' in the bottom-left rail), violating the brief's design rule of 'exactly one prominent action per view'.
findings.norm: A single view should have only one high-contrast primary CTA so the next step is unmistakable.
findings.fix: Keep 'Message Chief' as the sole solid-white primary button in the 'After connecting' state and render '+ New' in the dark glass surface treatment until the onboarding banner is dismissed.

findings.element: 'Space settings' screens ('Space settings, Personal', 'Space settings, Northwind', 'Delete space')
findings.problem: In Space settings, the save/confirm checkmark button ('✓') is placed at the bottom-left corner of the hardware rail—over 500pt away from the 'Name' text field at the top—and stays bright white even when no edits have been made. Additionally, 'Personal' lacks a 'Delete space' button with no helper text explaining why it cannot be deleted.
findings.norm: Form confirmation actions should be proximate to the form or in the top header and only active when changes are dirty; non-deletable default spaces should indicate their default status.
findings.fix: Move the save action inline or to the top-right header (enabled only when the name changes), remove the bottom-left '✓' FAB, and add a subtle caption under 'Personal' ('Default space cannot be deleted').

findings.element: 'Delete Northwind?' confirmation dialog in 'Delete space' state
findings.problem: The destructive confirmation alert floats directly beneath the 'Delete space' button without a full-screen dimming scrim, and is horizontally offset to the right because of the left rail, while the bottom-left '✓' button remains visible.
findings.norm: Destructive confirmation alerts on iOS must sit above a full-viewport dimmed backdrop and be visually centered within the active canvas.
findings.fix: Apply a full-screen dark scrim over the entire view (including the left rail) and center the 'Delete Northwind?' alert vertically and horizontally.

findings.element: Bottom of viewport in 'Home' (Main.png and PG-A-Home.png) and top of viewport in 'Scrolled to the end'
findings.problem: In the default Home state, PAGES is clipped mid-way through 'Legal' with 'Cap table', 'Data room', 'Team computer', and 'ARTIFACTS' hidden below the fold. When scrolled ('Scrolled to the end' in PG-A-Home.png), the 'Personal' space header scrolls completely off-screen and 'Mercury agent' collides with the top edge of the viewport at the same vertical level as the camera cutout.
findings.norm: Scrolling content must respect a sticky top header or top safe-area inset so users always know which Space they are in and list rows never collide with hardware cutouts.
findings.fix: Keep the Space title bar ('Personal v') pinned as a compact sticky header on scroll so the active space remains visible and scrolled rows clip cleanly below the header.

findings.element: Left navigation rail in PG-A-Activity.png vs. PG-A-Home.png
findings.problem: Tapping the Bell icon in the left rail opens 'Activity' (PG-A-Activity.png), which unexpectedly destroys the entire left navigation rail (Avatar, Bell, Search, '+ New') and replaces it with a single '<' back button. Furthermore, the Bell icon glyph in PG-A-Home.png has a static hollow circle on its top-right corner in every single state (even in 'Loading', 'Empty space', and 'New account, no model'), failing to distinguish when an agent actually 'Needs you'.
findings.norm: Persistent navigation rail items should either switch views in-place with an active state or use a dynamic badge that only appears when actionable notifications exist.
findings.fix: Use a high-contrast yellow/red notification dot on the Bell icon only when an activity item 'Needs you', and remove the static circle from the base bell icon in empty/loading states.

findings.element: 'PERSONNEL' list rows vs. 'ACTIVITY', 'PAGES', and 'ARTIFACTS' cards
findings.problem: While ACTIVITY, PAGES, and ARTIFACTS are grouped inside rounded dark-grey card containers with internal hairlines and right chevrons, PERSONNEL rows float directly on the pure-black background with no container, no dividers, and no chevrons. In state 7 ('Pinned, group, unread'), placing the unread dot to the right of the timestamp ('2:59 PM •') pushes the timestamps out of vertical alignment with read rows.
findings.norm: Sibling interactive list sections should share consistent surface grouping, and unread indicators must not cause right-aligned timestamps to jitter horizontally.
findings.fix: Place the unread dot in a fixed slot (either to the left of the timestamp or on the avatar/title) so all right-edge timestamps align vertically, and consider giving PERSONNEL the same card container treatment as adjacent sections.

findings.element: Inline network error message 'Check your connection and retry' in PG-B-NewBot.png, PG-B-NewGroup.png, and PG-B-NewSpace.png
findings.problem: While 'Error: name taken' in PG-B-NewSpace.png highlights the 'Name' input with a red border and places the error directly underneath the field, network errors ('Check your connection and retry') in all three creation sheets are placed as small red text at the very bottom-left of the sheet without an icon or border, far from the top-right 'Create' button the user just tapped.
findings.norm: Form-level submission errors should be visually prominent and distinguish between field validation errors and system/network errors.
findings.fix: Display network submission errors as a compact banner with an alert icon either directly below the sheet header or above the form fields so the user sees it immediately after tapping 'Create'.

findings.element: Background skeleton placeholders behind creation sheets in PG-B-NewBot.png, PG-B-NewGroup.png, and PG-B-NewSpace.png
findings.problem: When opening 'New bot', 'New group', or 'New space' from the Home screen, the underlying Home screen turns into abstract dark skeleton bars instead of showing the dimmed Home view (contradicting PG-A-HomeNoModel.png, where the real Home content remains visible behind the sheet).
findings.norm: Modal sheets presented over an existing loaded screen should dim the underlying screen rather than replacing loaded content with loading skeletons.
findings.fix: Show the actual underlying screen dimmed behind a dark scrim when presenting creation sheets, matching standard iOS sheet presentation.

findings.element: Color picker and avatar preview in PG-B-NewBot.png
findings.problem: In 'New bot', users choose from 7 circular color swatches (two of which are nearly identical oranges and two nearly identical indigo/purples), yet on the Home screen agents are distinguished by unique geometric shapes (hexagon, triangle, pill, droplet) or monogram letters ('C', 'M', 'B'). The creation sheet provides no preview of what the bot's avatar will look like.
findings.norm: Avatar/color customization controls should preview the resulting identity artifact and use clearly distinct color swatches.
findings.fix: Show a live preview of the bot avatar (shape or monogram with the selected color) in the 'New bot' sheet and increase perceptual contrast between the orange and purple swatch pairs.

findings.element: Activity rows without chevrons in PG-A-Home.png and PG-A-Activity.png
findings.problem: In both the Home 'ACTIVITY' card and the full 'Activity' screen, only the 'Finance agent' ('Needs you >') row has a trailing chevron, while 'Legal agent' ('Working'), 'Weekly runway' ('Done'), 'Inbox agent' ('Done'), and 'Brex agent' ('Done') have no chevron, making it unclear whether users can tap working or completed items to inspect their output.
findings.norm: If all activity rows open the agent chat or run log on tap, they should share consistent tap affordances.
findings.fix: Add subtle trailing chevrons to all tappable activity rows so the founder knows they can inspect completed work ('Sent your reply to Ana', 'Weekly runway') in one tap.

excellent: The outer-display hardware adaptation (466x678 pt) with a dedicated left-hand thumb strip below the camera cutout is clever, ergonomic, and respects the 'at most three glass groups' constraint.

Visual hierarchy on the Home screen ('Needs you' yellow badge at the top of Activity, clean typographic scale, high-contrast dark surfaces without muddy gradients) allows a founder to spot urgent approvals in under a second.

State coverage across the boards—including offline cached data ('Updated 5 min ago'), loading skeletons, partial section failure ('Could not load agents'), 0/1/2 member group validation, and duplicate space name errors—is thorough and thoughtfully structured.
